# Revamp status log

This is the append-only coordination log for the six revamp threads (`engine`, `providers`, `ui-core`, `ui-screens`, `platform`, `integrator`). One entry per line, newest at the bottom, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM | <thread> | <TYPE> | <lane> | text`, with local Mac time, the thread name in lower case as listed, and `-` as the lane when an entry is about the whole thread. TYPE is one of NOTICE, FROZEN, HANDOFF-READY, LANE-DONE, REQUEST, BLOCKED-ON, CONTRACT-CHANGE-PROPOSED, CONTRACT-CHANGE-DONE, SLIP, READY-FOR-OWNER, APPROVED, MERGED, DECIDED. Never edit or delete an entry, yours or anyone's; correct one by appending a new entry that says so. Read it before each work package and each PR (`git fetch origin revamp`, then `git show origin/revamp:plans/STATUS.md`). Add entries as tiny commits pushed straight to `revamp`: `git pull --no-rebase origin revamp`, append your line at the end of the log, commit, `git push origin HEAD:revamp`; if the push is refused, pull again and retry, never force. No secrets, tokens, real addresses or real mail in any entry. Path ownership is in [OWNERS.md](OWNERS.md); `node plans/tools/queue.mjs` prints the owner's review queue from this file and flags malformed entries; the schedule and the rules behind this file are in [00-roadmap.md](00-roadmap.md) sections 1, 4, 7 and 12.

## Entry text, by type

Keep entries to one line. Address a REQUEST or BLOCKED-ON to a thread or lane by starting the text with `to <thread or lane>:`.

- `DECIDED`: a question whose answer was clear or had a default in the plans, the answer, and a one-line reason. Use it instead of waiting for the owner (owner's standing instruction, 2026-10-27). Questions that need a sign-in click, money, a design taste call the specs don't settle, a feature approval or anything on the hard-rules list still go to the owner; block only that item.
- `SLIP`: what moved, from which day to which day, and what it moves downstream.
- `READY-FOR-OWNER`: `F<n> <feature name> | <link to the ready post in the T3 thread> | lanes: <lane>, <lane>`.
- `APPROVED`: `F<n> | <lane>@<sha>, <lane>@<sha> | snapshot saved`.
- `MERGED` (feature PRs): `F<n> | <PR URL> | nothing material changed since <sha> | owner told`. The Integrator checks that an earlier READY-FOR-OWNER and APPROVED exist for the same feature and reverts the merge if not.
- `MERGED` (dependency and infrastructure PRs, posted by the integrator): `<PR URL> | <one-line summary>`.
- `CONTRACT-CHANGE-PROPOSED`: what is added and why, and the PR URL once it exists.

## How a PR gets into `revamp`

Every lane opens its PR from `rv/<lane>/<slug>` into `revamp`, after merging `revamp` into its branch. Nobody merges into `main`, ever.

1. **Dependency and infrastructure PRs** (anything another lane's "Needs" column names, and every PR from `eng-contract`, `eng-store`, `eng-views`, `prov-emu`, `ui-foundation`, `plat-ci` and `plat-release`) are merged by the integrator only. Before merging, the integrator confirms:
   - the PR touches only its lane's paths (the owners check, `scripts/audit/owners-check.mjs` once it lands; by hand against OWNERS.md until then);
   - `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run check` pass at the PR head merged with current `revamp` (`npm run check` once `plat-ci` adds it);
   - the conformance suite passes on the stand-in engine, and the real-engine run fails only on its expected-fail list, which may shrink and never grow (once the suite exists);
   - the evidence (test output, numbers, screenshots where relevant) is attached to the PR, never committed;
   - an agent that did not write the code has reviewed it.
   - the PR says which models wrote its code (roadmap 5.1a). Code written by a free OpenCode model or a Cursor model merges only with passing tests and a review of the full diff by a Claude agent; without that review the integrator refuses the merge.
   Small PRs merge in arrival order, critical lanes first when several wait (`eng-store`, `prov-gmail`, `eng-views`, `ui-shell`, `ui-reader`). Squash merge, except Phase 0's mechanical restructure commits, which merge by merge commit and go into `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.
2. **Feature PRs** follow the same model rule, then the per-feature loop (roadmap 12.3): READY-FOR-OWNER, the owner's approval, APPROVED with SHAs, four deep review passes, the PR with `gh pr create --attach`, then the lead thread squash-merges it itself only if nothing material changed since the approval snapshot, and posts MERGED. After every feature merge the integrator runs the full suite, the conformance run and the owners check on `revamp`.
3. **Never self-merged:** any PR labelled `contract-change` (the integrator merges it), a PR that touches another lane's paths, and anything that would merge while `revamp` is red. Post a REQUEST to the integrator instead. A PR that touches `packages/contract/**`, `packages/engine/src/ports.ts`, `packages/engine/src/store/migrations/**` or `packages/engine/src/methods/index.ts` from any lane other than `eng-contract` (or `eng-store` for migrations) is refused. Contract changes are additive within `v:1`.
4. **Red `revamp`:** the integrator finds the PR that broke it and reverts that PR at once with a note to its lane. Nobody force-pushes a shared branch; fix forward or revert.

In plain words: the probe wrote a draft whose raw message carried OUR Message-ID header (`<aplos-live-probe-YYYYMMDD@aplos.invalid>`), then read the draft's Message-ID back with drafts.get (metadata): it was NOT equal to ours straight after `drafts.create` (createKeptMessageId = 0, an exact string comparison), the draft id survives an API save and the message id changes on every save (as designed), and the header after the second save is also not ours. So on real Gmail the Message-ID header of a draft is NOT the one we upload (Gmail assigns its own, or drops ours); we do not yet know what it is replaced with, or whether Gmail's value is stable across a save or a phone edit (the probe only compares to OURS). Consequence if this holds for the engine's real uploads (it should: same drafts.create/update path): everything that rests on OUR Message-ID surviving on the provider copy is dead on real Gmail: `findByInternetId` (the `rfc822msgid:` search after a lost reply), `adoptCopy`'s Message-ID proof, `isEcho`'s Message-ID match, `supersedes`/`earlier` and the create-conflict adoption: a lost-reply create would leave a DUPLICATE and the engine would never recognise its own copy by id (the content fingerprint proof from #194 still works but only once a copy is found). It also means the emulator's behaviour (it keeps the Message-ID) is wrong for this rule: the Gmail emulator must stop preserving it (and its tests must then prove the engine copes). NOT a code change today (the real path is off), but it is the biggest open design risk for draft sync on Gmail and must be settled BEFORE APLOS_ENGINE=real is turned on. Next measurements (REQUEST below): is a custom header (`X-Aplos-Draft: <opaque id>`) preserved by drafts.create/update and visible via drafts.get? is Gmail's own Message-ID stable across API saves and a phone edit? does `rfc822msgid:` / a header search find a draft by Gmail's id?

MEDIUM reporter.ts:165 (new w.ResizeObserver(watch)) with 143-151: the sub-pixel/width wiggle is NOT fixed, only halved. Example from your own DECISIONS: body{animation:w .5s infinite alternate} 50% to 60% width with constant height: the observer fires every rendered frame, every call arms one look (getBoundingClientRect + two getComputedStyle + a 250 ms timer); over 6,000 frames this PR does 6,000 looks and 1 post (origin/revamp does 12,000 looks), and the 2,000 cap never engages because only POSTS count. DECISIONS says "a look that finds nothing lets the loop sleep": it does, and the observer wakes it on the next frame. FIX (either): after a look that found no change, let the observer and animation events arm ONLY the timer (not the animation frame), which caps those looks at about 4 a second; or add a lifetime budget on LOOKS (say 100,000) next to the post cap; and correct the DECISIONS text either way. Add a unit test for the width-wiggle (looks stay bounded). LOW 1: "without a clock a look never re-arms" is false: with now() = -Infinity the per-second counter never resets (time - since >= 1000 is never true), so after 20 posts every change is held back and the held-back flag re-arms a look every frame forever (1,000 idle frames = 1,000 looks, height stuck 690 vs true 750); your test uses frames:false which removes the frames and timers so it never reaches this. Unreachable in Electron (performance always exists) but fix it: skip the rate limit when time is not finite, and test with frames on. LOW 2: cumulative window or sidebar dragging can exhaust the 2,000 cap (a resize drag posts up to 20/s; about 100 s of dragging over a frame's life, after which a later width is never reported and the letter is clipped or gapped): do not count (or reset total) when the frame width w changed, since the host sets the width and the letter cannot game it. Informational, no action: off screen each look leaves a stale rAF callback queued (about 401 after 100 s, bounded by the cap, no-ops later); about 15 timers are pending during a watch, so "one timer at a time" is wrong in the docs but harmless. Push the fix, name both SWE-2 passes' findings in the READY, and I run the check and a short delta pass (not a full second Opus round) before merging.

Today nothing outside the store and tests sets startUtc (grep: only store/calendar.ts, store/port.ts and tests), so the real Google calendar writer, when it lands, will produce exactly such rows and every one of the owner's single events would silently vanish from the Calendar. (2) All-day (date) and floating events have no zone of their own; their stored UTC instants are the date at UTC midnight, but the view reads them in the VIEWER's zone (instant(base.start, env.zone)), up to +-14 h away, so an all-day event on the first or last day of the window can fall just outside an exact [from, to) comparison and be dropped; and a zero-length event at exactly from fails end_utc > from. This is why my #315 ticket said a +-2 day margin. FIX: AND (e.recurrence_id != '' OR e.recurrence IS NOT NULL OR e.start_utc IS NULL OR e.end_utc IS NULL OR (e.start_utc < ? + 172800000 AND e.end_utc >= ? - 172800000)) with the two params as spec.to and spec.from (the in-JS window logic still decides what is actually in range, so the margin only costs a few extra rows). (3) A write on an account without it fails `permission` with body.reasonCode `permission.calendarWrite` (plain sentence in body.message) and the account then carries `missingPermissions` [{capability:'calendarWrite', reasonCode:'permission.calendarWrite', missingScopes:[calendar.events]}]: show "Turn on editing" with the Enable editing action, do not show it as an error banner and do not add a standing nag for read-only accounts. Add copy for `permission.calendarWrite`. (4) New event: `Event/set {opId, change:{type:'create', calendarId, fields:{title,start,end,allDay,timeZone?,location?,description?,attendees?}}, notify?}`; floating times need `timeZone` (on the field or `fields.timeZone`) else `validation` event.timeZoneRequired; all-day uses `date` times (end exclusive, as Google). (5) Edit: `Event/set {change:{type:'update', id, scope:'occurrence'|'series', fields:<only changed>}, notify?}`; id of one occurrence is `<seriesId>@<recurrenceId>` (scope occurrence makes an exception, series edits the master); switching allDay needs start and end together. `following` is `unsupported` (event.followingUnsupported): do not offer "this and following". (6) Delete: `Event/set {change:{type:'destroy', id, scope}}`; deleting an occurrence leaves a cancelled exception. (7) RSVP: `Event/rsvp {opId, id, response:'accepted'|'tentative'|'declined', scope, notify?}` (default tells the organizer; `validation` event.notAGuest when the owner is not a guest). (8) Errors by body.reasonCode: `calendar.conflict` (type conflict: changed elsewhere, the newer copy is already in the store, re-open the editor on it), `calendar.readOnly` (type unsupported: hide edit actions on calendars with Calendar.readOnly), `calendar.uncertain` (answer lost: tell the owner to check the calendar, do not auto-retry), `calendar.unavailable` (nothing changed, retryAfterMs may be set), `calendar.eventGone`, `calendar.forbidden` (event belongs to someone else), `calendar.rejected`. (9) Receipts are `undoable:false` and the event row updates when the call returns (write-through, no optimistic overlay, no undo window yet; a follow-up PR will add them, I will post the shape). Session.capabilities.calendarWrite is true for the engine; per-account truth is (1).

2026-11-10 13:58 | eng-contract | DECIDED | providers, integrator-3 | calendarHolds seam, decided here because no eng-views thread is live (integrator-3 may overrule; methods/operation.ts stays eng-views' file, so its PR needs lane-approved:eng-views from integrator-3): YES to the shape, with retry in it. Interface: services.calendarHolds { has(opId): boolean; get(opIds): Operation[]; undo(args, caller): Receipt; retry(args, caller): Receipt }, a HostPorts/lane service like aiTransport (optional, absent = no holds, methods/operation.ts behaves exactly as today). methods/operation.ts: undo and retry go to calendarHolds when has(opId), else threadOps; get splits the ids, asks each side for its own, and returns one list with notFound = ids neither knows. Rules the hold must keep: scopeRule 'originating' (record the originating method's scope, check it in undo/retry as threadOps does), get returns the contract Operation shape (a held write reads queued until the window ends, failed afterwards if the provider refused, so the inline Retry exists), undo cancels while held (undoUntil) and otherwise queues the inverse under undoOpId, never a delayed commit (the Operation/undo summary). Retry is therefore offered for calendar ops, not documented away: a failed calendar write is a contract 'failed' operation and the UI shows Retry for every failed op. No contract change. prov-cal: you may open the methods/operation.ts + services PR; ask integrator-3 for lane-approved:eng-views, and I will review the runtime/services.ts line for eng-contract.
